profile.name: Naz elama
profile.tagline: A traditional Azerbaijani couple dance depicting playful romantic resistance.
profile.insight: In 1989, dancers Shafiga Hanifayeva and Kamil Dadashov brought this Azerbaijani performance to Czechoslovakia, showcasing a dance whose title translates to "Don't be capricious."
profile.profile: Naz elama is a national Azerbaijani dance performed by a man and a woman. The dance requires high levels of expressiveness and refinement to portray the theme of romantic caprice. It gained international prominence through the performances of Amina Dilbazi, who considered it her signature piece.
profile.profile_long: Naz elama is a traditional Azerbaijani folk dance characterized by its focus on the interaction between a male and female partner. The title of the dance, which translates from Azerbaijani as "Don't be capricious," dictates the emotional tone and performance style required of the dancers. It is a performance that demands a high degree of expressiveness, refinement, and impetuosity to effectively communicate the theme of romantic resistance or playfulness between the couple. The dance achieved significant popularity through the work of the artist Amina Dilbazi, who performed it extensively throughout her career. Dilbazi referred to the dance as her crowning number, noting that she traveled all over the world with it. The dance was also featured in the musical film "The labour and rose," directed by Tofig Taghizade and dedicated to the People’s Artist of the USSR, Makhmud Esambayev. In this film, Esambayev performs the dance alongside Amina Dilbazi. The reach of the tradition is further evidenced by international performances, such as the 1989 appearance by Shafiga Hanifayeva and Kamil Dadashov in Czechoslovakia. While the dance remains a recognized part of the Azerbaijani national repertoire, specific technical details regarding its choreography, musical structure, and costume requirements are not documented in the sources.

sections.origins_and_history: The dance is a national Azerbaijani folk dance. It gained prominence in the 20th century, particularly through the performances of Amina Dilbazi and its inclusion in the musical film 'The labour and rose'.
sections.occasions_and_meaning: The title translates to 'Don't be capricious,' which is reflected in the expressive and impetuous nature of the performance.
sections.notable_figures: Amina Dilbazi, Makhmud Esambayev, Shafiga Hanifayeva, Kamil Dadashov, Khanlar Bashirov, Jamila Bayramova.
